name: companion
description: An opt-in day companion: reminders that actually go off, a watchlist that speaks up when a folder really changes, and a day plan you can ask for. Three surfaces, each switched on separately, and all three off out of the box — installing this app arms nothing. Its automations are served to the Automations page from this app's own store and are never written into PersonalClaw's, so turning a surface off, disabling the app or uninstalling it removes every trigger it contributed. Every one of them raises a notification and nothing else: this app deliberately never authors an automation that runs a prompt, a workflow or an agent, so a reminder's text can never become a scheduled instruction.
author: PersonalClaw

x-meta.label: Reminders
x-meta.help: Off by default. On, companion_remind can add reminders and each pending one becomes an automation that raises a notification at its time. Off, the tool declines and every reminder automation disappears — the reminders themselves are kept, so switching back on restores them.

x-meta.label: Watchlist
x-meta.help: Off by default. On, companion_watch can add a file, folder or 'folder/*.ext' glob, and each one becomes an automation that notifies when its contents really change. Off, the tool declines and every watch automation disappears.

x-meta.label: Day brief at
x-meta.help: A 24-hour time like '08:30' to be nudged once a day to plan; empty means off. The nudge is a notification — the plan itself is rendered by companion_day_plan, in a session you are present for.

x-meta.label: Timezone
x-meta.help: IANA name, e.g. 'Europe/Berlin'. Empty reads the machine's zone from /etc/localtime, and falls back to UTC if that cannot be determined — which matters, because an unset zone means your 08:30 reminder fires at 08:30 UTC. `personalclaw doctor` reports the zone actually in use.
